{{Use dmy dates|date=July 2021}} {{Use Hiberno-English|date=July 2021}} {{Infobox football match | title = 2014 Munster Senior Hurling Championship final | image = | event = [[2014 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship#Munster Senior Hurling Championship|2014 Munster Senior Hurling Championship]] | team1 = {{GG|Cork|hurling}} | team1association = [[File:Cork colours.PNG|40px]] | team1score = 2-24 | team2 = {{GG|Limerick|hurling}} | team2association = [[File:Limerick colours.PNG|40px]] | team2score = 0-24 | details = | date = 13 July 2014 | stadium = [[Páirc Uí Chaoimh]] | city = [[Cork City|Cork]] | man_of_the_match1a = [[Séamus Harnedy]] | referee = [[Brian Gavin (referee)|Brian Gavin]] (Offaly) | attendance = 36,075 | weather = Sunshine (20°C) | previous = [[2013 Munster Senior Hurling Championship final|2013]] | next = [[2015 Munster Senior Hurling Championship final|2015]] }} The '''2014 Munster Senior Hurling Championship final''' was the 123rd final of the [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship]], the most prestigious provincial [[hurling]] championship. The match, contested by defending champions [[Limerick county hurling team|Limerick]] and [[Cork county hurling team|Cork]], took place on 13 July 2014 at [[Páirc Uí Chaoimh]] in [[Cork (city)|Cork]], and started at 4:00 p.m.{{cite web|url = http://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/cork-given-green-light-to-host-munster-hurling-final-at-pairc-ui-chaoimh-30382120.html|title=Cork given green light to host Munster hurling final at Pairc Ui Chaoimh |date=25 June 2014|work=Irish Independent|accessdate=25 June 2014}} The final also marked the last major GAA match at Páirc Uí Chaoimh before a €70 million redevelopment.{{cite web|url = http://www.irishtimes.com/sport/gaelic-games/p%C3%A1irc-u%C3%AD-chaoimh-gets-green-light-to-stage-munster-hurling-final-1.1843978|title= Páirc Uí Chaoimh gets green light to stage Munster hurling final|date=25 June 2014|work=Irish Times|accessdate=25 June 2014}}{{cite web|url = http://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/hurling/10-reasons-why-you-cant-miss-this-munster-final-274951.html|title=10 reasons why you can’t miss this Munster final|date=10 July 2014|work= Irish Examiner |accessdate=10 July 2014}} The championship winners were awarded a place in the [[List of All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship semi-finals|semi-finals]] of the [[2014 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]] on 17 August, while the loser went through to the [[List of All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship quarter-finals|quarter-finals]] on 27 July. Cork won their first Munster title since 2006 after a 2-24 to 0-24 win.{{cite web|url = http://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/supersub-paudie-osullivan-gives-cork-real-belief-30428526.html|title=Supersub Paudie O'Sullivan gives Cork real belief|date=14 July 2014|work= Irish Independent|accessdate=14 July 2014}}{{cite web|url = http://www.irishmirror.ie/sport/gaa/hurling/hurling-match-reports/cork-beat-limerick-claim-first-3851089|title=Cork beat Limerick to claim first Munster title in eight years|date=14 July 2014|work= Irish Mirror|accessdate=14 July 2014}}{{cite web|url=http://www.thescore.ie/cork-limerick-munster-senior-hurling-final-1569197-Jul2014/|title=As It Happened: Cork v Limerick, Munster senior hurling final|date=14 July 2014|work=The Score|accessdate=14 July 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140715151301/http://www.thescore.ie/cork-limerick-munster-senior-hurling-final-1569197-Jul2014/|archive-date=2014-07-15|url-status=dead}} ==Route to the final== ===Cork=== {{football box collapsible | date = 25 May 2014 | round = Quarter-final | time = 14:00 | team1 = [[Waterford county hurling team|Waterford]] | score = 1-21 - 1-21 | team2 = [[Cork county hurling team|Cork]] | report = http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/hurling/2014/0525/619564-cork-1-21-waterford-1-21/ | goals1 = P Mahony (0-11, 0-09 f), A Gleeson (1-02), B O’Sullivan (0-02), B Coughlan (0-01), J Nagle (0-01), T de Búrca (0-01), J Dillon (0-01), S Walsh (0-01), E Barrett (0-01). | goals2 = P Horgan (0-12, 0-08 frees 0-01 ’65), B Cooper (1-01), A Cadogan (0-04), A Walsh (0-02), C Lehane (0-01), S Harnedy (0-01). | stadium = [[Semple Stadium]] | referee = B Gavin (Offaly) | attendance = 16,025 }} {{football box collapsible | date = 8 June 2014 | round = Quarter-final

2-18 | team2 = [[Limerick county hurling team|Limerick]] | report = http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/hurling/2014/0601/620990-tipperary-v-limerick/ | goals1 = G Ryan (1-02), J O’Dwyer, (0-05, 1f) S Callanan (0-05, 3f), Patrick Maher (1-00), N McGrath (0-01), N O'Meara (0-01), L Corbett (0-01), D Maher (0-01). | goals2 = S Dowling (2-09, 1-09f), D O’Grady (0-02), K Downes (0-02), P Browne (0-01), D Hannon (0-01), G Mulcahy (0-01), S Hickey (0-01), T Ryan (0-01). | stadium = [[Semple Stadium]] | referee = B Kelly (Westmeath) | attendance = 24,912 }} ==Build-up== Tickets for the game were initially only available for purchase from clubs, with no public sale. The capacity of Páirc Uí Chaoimh for the match was announced at 32,168. Covered stand tickets were priced at €35, with uncovered stand tickets at €30 and terrace tickets at €20.{{cite web|url= http://munster.gaa.ie/2014/07/07/munster-gaa-senior-hurling-championship-final/|title= Munster Senior Hurling Final – Limerick v Cork|date= 7 July 2014|work= Munster GAA|accessdate= 8 July 2014|archive-url= https://archive.today/20140709152748/http://munster.gaa.ie/2014/07/07/munster-gaa-senior-hurling-championship-final/|archive-date= 2014-07-09|url-status= dead}} The match was shown live on [[RTÉ Two]] as part of ''[[The Sunday Game|The Sunday Game Live]]'', presented by [[Michael Lyster]], with match commentary from [[Ger Canning]] and [[Michael Duignan (hurler)|Michael Duignan]] and studio analysis from [[Cyril Farrell]], [[Ger Loughnane]] and [[Liam Sheedy]]. On 10 July, following the completion of works at the grounds, the capacity for the final was increased to 36,646, with extra tickets being made available.{{cite web|url = http://www1.skysports.com/hurling/news/12040/9377791/gaa-p225irc-u237-chaoimh-capacity-increased-to-36646-for-sundays-munster-shc-final|title= GAA: Páirc Uí Chaoimh capacity increased to 36,646 for Sunday's Munster SHC final|date=10 July 2014|work= Sky Sports|accessdate=10 July 2014}} 1,500 terrace tickets for the Blackrock and City Ends were made available for purchase via tickets.ie and selected Centra and SuperValu stores on 10 July, however technical issues concerning tickets.ie, prevented supporters from purchasing tickets both in person and online.{{cite web|url = http://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/fans-see-red-after-tickets-fiasco-275130.html|title=Fans see red after tickets fiasco|date=11 July 2014|work= Irish Examiner|accessdate=11 July 2014}} Cork last won the Munster championship in [[2006 Munster Senior Hurling Championship final|2006]], the longest gap since the 10-year period between their 1956 and 1966 wins. Limerick's last title was in [[2013 Munster Senior Hurling Championship final|2013]], when they defeated Cork by 0-24 to 0-15.{{cite web|url = http://www.limerickleader.ie/sport/limerick-sport/munster-final-last-five-limerick-v-cork-championship-meetings-1-6170081|title= Munster Final - Last five Limerick v Cork championship meetings|date=11 July 2014|work= Limerick Leader|accessdate=11 July 2014}} This was the 23rd meeting between Cork and Limerick in a Munster Final, with Cork having won 14 and Limerick winning 6, with 2 drawn finals in 1940 and 1944. Cork's last Munster final win against Limerick was in 1992 when they won by 1-22 to 3-11 at [[Semple Stadium]]. Cork aimed to win their 52nd Munster title, with Limerick going for their 20th title. [[Brian Gavin (referee)|Brian Gavin]] refereed his third Munster senior hurling final, he previously took charge of the 2010 replay and the 2011 final.{{cite web|url=http://munster.gaa.ie/2014/07/07/munster-gaa-senior-hurling-championship-final/|title=2014 Munster Hurling Final|date=11 July 2014|work=Munster GAA|accessdate=11 July 2014|archive-url=https://archive.today/20140709152748/http://munster.gaa.ie/2014/07/07/munster-gaa-senior-hurling-championship-final/|archive-date=2014-07-09|url-status=dead}} ==Team selection== Limerick made one change to their team for the final, with [[David Breen]] coming in to replace [[Seán Tobin]] at corner forward.{{cite web|url =http://thescore.thejournal.ie/limerick-team-cork-munster-hurling-final-cork-1565045-Jul2014/|title=Limerick bring in Breen for Munster showdown with Cork|date=11 July 2014|work= The Score|accessdate=11 July 2014}} Limerick were managed by [[T. price for all those strikes – Cronin |date=9 July 2014|work= Irish Independent|accessdate=11 July 2014}} ==Match== ===Summary=== Limerick made the better start and were 0-8 to 0-4 ahead by the 21st minute. Cork came back to level at 0-8 apiece and then went 0-12 to 0-9 in front approaching half time. The sides were level at 0-12 to 0-12 at halftime. The sides were level at 0-18 apiece midway through the second-half when [[Séamus Harnedy]] ran in on goals to score the opening goal in the 55th minute. Paudie O’Sullivan got the second goal of the game with five minutes remaining when he caught a ball from Daniel Kearney before finishing low to the net. Cork eventually ran out winners by six points.{{cite web|url = http://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/hurling/irrepressible-rebels-rule-munster-again-275363.html|title= Irrepressible Rebels rule Munster again|date=14 July 2014|work= Irish Examiner|accessdate=14 July 2014}}{{cite web|url = http://www.hoganstand.com/ArticleForm.aspx?ID=220356|title= Munster SHC final: Rebels reclaim crown at Limerick's expense|date=14 July 2014|work= Hogan Stand|accessdate=14 July 2014}} ===Details=== {{football box |date = 13 July 2014 |time = 16:00 [[Irish Summer Time|IST]] |team1 = {{GG|Cork|hurling}} |score = 2-24 - Cork manager Jimmy Barry-Murphy felt that the victory was just reward for the efforts his Cork side had put in over the previous few seasons, saying "I'm very proud of the players and just thrilled for them and their families, they have made a massive effort over the last couple of years. We knew ourselves we had won nothing; we lost two finals last year and that was tough, It's a great reward for the players and the efforts they've made."{{cite web|url = http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/hurling/2014/0713/630538-jbm-winning-s/|title=Jimmy Barry-Murphy Players deserved a Munster title|date=14 July 2014|work= RTÉ Sport|accessdate=14 July 2014}}{{cite web|url= http://www.thescore.ie/jimmy-barry-murphy-rebels-1570226-Jul2014/|title= After the ‘bitter pills’ of defeat in 2013, delight at last in a final for JBM and Cork|date= 14 July 2014|work= The Score|accessdate= 14 July 2014|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20140716111422/http://www.thescore.ie/jimmy-barry-murphy-rebels-1570226-Jul2014/|archive-date= 2014-07-16|url-status= dead}} Limerick manager TJ Ryan felt two big turnovers in the second half went a long way to deciding the game, saying "We are very disappointed, Munster finals are there for winning. We would love to have won it but it wasn't to be," said Ryan with a shake of his head, I think Cork just edged it in the finish and got some good scores and the first goal was always going to be crucial. We had some half chances in the first half and they got the chance in the second half and took it".{{cite web|url = http://www.limerickleader.ie/sport/limerick-sport/tj-ryan-rues-missed-limerick-chances-1-6176388|title= TJ Ryan rues missed Limerick chances|date=14 July 2014|work= Limerick Leader|accessdate=14 July 2014}} ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== {{Munster Senior Hurling Championship}} {{GAA 2014}} [[Category:2014 in hurling|Munster]] [[Category:Munster Senior Hurling Championship finals]] [[Category:Cork county hurling team matches]] [[Category:Hurling competitions in County Cork]] [[Category:Sport in Cork (city)]] [[Category:July 2014 sports events in Ireland]] [[Category:Limerick county hurling team matches]]
